subsystems.name: Optical engine
subsystems.role: draws a virtual image onto the user's palm instead of using a screen.
parts: red, green and blue laser diodes (or a single green diode)

subsystems.name: Depth and camera sensing
subsystems.role: finds the palm, focuses the projection and reads the environment.

subsystems.name: Compute and connectivity
subsystems.role: runs the assistant locally and offloads heavy models to the cloud.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: fits enough energy into a badge-sized body without burning the wearer.

subsystems.name: Agent software
subsystems.role: turns camera, microphone and location into useful answers.
parts: multimodal model running in the cloud
phone and web app for settings

subsystems.name: Enclosure and mounting
subsystems.role: keeps the device on clothing and aimed at the hand.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical path
buildSteps.detail: Choose laser wavelengths and scan angles so that a readable image lands on a palm 20–40 cm away, then model distortion and speckle in software.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the MEMS mirror
buildSteps.detail: A silicon-on-insulator wafer is etched to leave a tiny suspended mirror on torsion springs, coated with a reflective layer, and diced and packaged in a vacuum or inert atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the optical engine
buildSteps.detail: Laser diodes, collimators and the scanning mirror are aligned to within a few micrometres in a clean room, then sealed against dust.

buildSteps.title: Build the electronics
buildSteps.detail: The system-on-chip, depth sensor, camera, cellular modem and microphones are mounted on a dense circuit board small enough to sit in the housing.

buildSteps.title: Solve thermal and power
buildSteps.detail: Heat paths are designed so skin-contact surfaces stay below roughly 43 °C, and the battery is sized against the measured power draw of camera, modem and projector together.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate each unit
buildSteps.detail: Because every laser and mirror differs slightly, each device is measured on a test rig and given its own correction table so the projected image is the right shape and colour.

buildSteps.title: Write the agent stack
buildSteps.detail: Camera frames, speech and location are streamed to a cloud model that returns text and actions; latency budgets, wake-word detection and privacy handling are tuned on real users.

buildSteps.title: Certify and support
buildSteps.detail: The projector must pass laser-safety rules such as IEC 60825-1 as a Class 1 product, plus radio and battery approvals, before shipping — and cloud services must be funded for the life of the device.

prerequisites.why: tiny MEMS mirrors scanned by laser diodes are already built at scale for head-up and pico projectors.
the assistant is only usable if vision, speech and answer return in about a second over a mobile network.
the device has no screen and no phone tether, so it needs its own cheap data connection.

prerequisites.tech: Skin-safe thermal design in sealed wearables
prerequisites.why: a fanless device against the body must shed several watts while staying comfortable to wear.
the projector must cut out instantly if a face enters the beam path to remain legally Class 1.

pathway.milestone: the first commercial screenless projector wearable shipped in 2024 and its cloud service was shut down in early 2025
pathway.unlocks: hard evidence that latency, battery life, projection brightness in daylight and a subscription price all matter more than novelty.

pathway.milestone: AI glasses that pair cameras, speakers and near-eye displays with a phone
pathway.unlocks: ambient assistance that people actually wear daily, with the display moved from the palm to the lens.

pathway.milestone: small on-device models handling speech and vision locally
pathway.unlocks: sub-second responses and offline use, which removes the biggest complaint about cloud-only wearables.

pathway.milestone: assistants spread across earbuds, glasses and a projector that shares one identity and context
pathway.unlocks: genuinely ambient computing, where the interface is chosen by situation rather than fixed to one gadget.
